senses.gloss:
शुंशुमार शुंशुमार, अस्, m. a porpoise,
(more usually written शिशु-मार, q. v.)
शुन् शुन्, cl. 6. P. शुनति, &c., to go.

शुन शुन, अस्, आ, अम् (probably fr. rt. श्वि),
white, pure, bright (Ved.; cf. श्वेत); causing pros-
perity or happiness, auspicious (Ved.); (अम्), ind.
happily, auspiciously (Ved.; Sāy. = सुखम्); (अस्),
m., N. of Vāyu (Ved.); a dog, (fr. श्वन्.)
—शुन-
होत्र, अस्, m., N. of the author of the hymns Ṛg-
veda VI. 33, 34 (having the patronymic Bhārad-
vāja).
—शुनासीरीय or शुनासीर्य, अम्, n. a par-
ticular sacrificial oblation (said to be offered in the
thirteenth month or Mala-māsa, and probably in
honour of Śuna and Sīra).
—शुना-सीरौ, m. du.,
Ved. Śuna and Sīra, N. of two Vedic gods (addressed
in Ṛg-veda IV. 57, and identified by Yāska with
Vāyu and Āditya; according to other authorities
Indra and Vāyu or Indra and Sūrya are meant; but
according to another view Sīra may perhaps denote
‘a ploughshare,’ and Śuna some part of a plough).
—शुनेषित (˚ना-इष्˚), अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. (probably)
borne along or carried by dogs.

शून शून, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. rt. श्वि, q. v.),
swelled, swollen, increased, grown, prospered; mor-
bidly swollen; empty, vacant (Ved., Sāy. = शून्य);
(अम्), n., Ved. swelling, increase, (Sāy. = सम्-ऋद्-
धि, Ṛg-veda III. 33, 13); emptiness, poverty, (Sāy.
= शून्य, दारिद्र्य, Ṛg-veda II. 27, 17); an in-
correct pronunciation (in Vedic phonetics).
शून, अस्, आ, अम्, swollen, &c. See s. v.

शूना शूना, f. (= सूना, q. v.), the uvula
or soft palate; a slaughter-house, any place where
animals are killed or are liable to be destroyed, (five
of these are enumerated, viz. a fire-place, a grind-
stone, a broom, a mortar, and a water-pot; cf.
पञ्च-सूना.)
—शूना-चक्र-ध्वज-वत्, आन्, अती,
अत्, one who keeps a slaughter-house, one who has
an oil-press, and one who exhibits a vintner's sign,
(Manu IV. 84.)
—शूना-दोष, see सूना-दोष.
—शूना-वत्, आन्, m. one who keeps a slaughter-
house, a butcher.
—शूना-स्थ, अस्, आ, अम्, being in
or brought from a slaughter-house or any place where
animals are destroyed.

सून, अस्, आ, अम्, born, produced; blown, blos-
somed, budded (as a flower); empty, vacant, (in this
sense probably for शून and शून्य); (आ), f. a
daughter, (for सूना, a slaughter-house, &c., see s. v.);
(अम्), n. bringing forth, parturition; a bud, blossom,
flower; [cf. प्र-सून.]
सून सून, सूनु. See p. 1118, col. 2.

सूना सूना, f. (in Uṇādi-s. III. 13. said to
be fr. rt. 3. सु), any place where animals are killed
or sacrificed; any place or utensil in a house where
animals are liable to be accidentally destroyed, (of
five kinds, see शूना, पञ्च-सूना); a slaughter-
house; killing, hurting, injuring [cf. सूदन]; the
sale of flesh or meat; the uvula or soft palate, (in
this and the next sense perhaps connected with
शून); inflammation of the glands of the neck
(commonly called mumps); a zone, girdle (according
to some); a ray (according to some); a river (ac-
cording to some).
—सूना-दोष, अस्, m. the guilt
incurred by destroying animals in any of the five
Sūnās, (see above; cf. Manu III. 71.)

शुनः-पुच्छ, अस्, m. (properly fr. शुनः, gen.
c. of श्वन् + पुच्छ), ‘dog-tailed,’ N. of one of the
three sons of Ṛcīka (or according to the Aitareya-
[]
Brāhmaṇa the eldest of the three sons of Ajīgarta);
N. of the author of a law-book.

शुनः-शेप or शुनः-शेफ, अस्, m. (शुनः,
gen. c. of श्वन्), ‘dog-tailed,’ N. of a Vedic Ṛṣi
(having the patronymic Ājigarti, as son of Ajigarta
or Ajīgarta, and regarded as the author of the hymns
Ṛg-veda I. 24-30, IX. 3; according to a legend
told in the Aitareya-Brāhmaṇa VII. 13-18, king
Hariścandra, whose priest was Viśvā-mitra, being
childless, made a vow that on obtaining a son he
would sacrifice him to the god Varuṇa; a son was
then born to him named Rohita, but Hariścandra
put off on various pretexts the fulfilment of his vow,
and when he at length consented to perform it, his
son declined being sacrificed, and retiring to the
forest passed six years there until he met a poor
Brāhman Ṛṣi named Ajīgarta, who had three sons,
the second of whom, Śunaḥ-śepha, was purchased by
Rohita for a hundred cows to serve as a substitute
for himself; Varuṇa having accepted him as a ransom,
he was about to be sacrificed, Viśvā-mitra being Hotṛ
priest, when he saved himself by reciting verses in
praise of various deities, and was received into the
family of Viśvā-mitra as one of his sons under the
name of Deva-rāta, q. v.: the legend is different in
the Rāmāyaṇa, which makes Ambarīṣa, king of
Ayodhyā, perform a sacrifice, the victim of which is
stolen by Indra; this king is described as wandering
over the earth in search of either the real victim or
a substitute until he meets with a Brāhman named
Ṛcīka, from whom he purchases his middle son,
Śunaḥ-śepha, who is about to be sacrificed, when
Viśvā-mitra saves him by teaching him a prayer to
Agni and two hymns to Indra and Viṣṇu; see
Rāmāyaṇa I. 61, 62); (अम्), n. the genital organ
of a dog.

शुनक, अस्, m. a young dog; a dog; N. of a
descendant of Bhṛgu; (आस्), m. pl., N. of a family;
[cf. शौनक.]
—शुनक-चञ्चुका, f. a kind of
plant (= क्षुद्र-चञ्चु).
—शुनक-चिल्ली, f. a kind
of pot-herb (= श्वान-चिल्लिका).
—शुनक-पुत्र,
अस्, m. the son of Śunaka, i. e. Śaunaka, (also applied
to Gṛtsamada, who is elsewhere described as the
father of Śunaka.)

शुनाशीर or शुनासीर, अस्, m., N. of Indra, (also
written सुनासीर, q. v., cf. शुना-सीरौ under शुन.)

सुनाशीर सुनाशीर or सुनासीर, अस्, m., N.
of Indra; [cf. शुनासीरौ.]
शुनि, इस्, m. (fr. श्वन्), a dog.

शुनी, f. a female dog, bitch, (see under श्वन्);
a kind of gourd (= कुष्माण्डी).
—शुनिन्-धम,
see Vopa-deva XXVI. 54.
—शुनिन्-धय, अस्, ई,
अम् (शुनि for शुनी), sucking a bitch, suckled by a
bitch.
शुनीर, अस्, m. a number of female dogs.

शुनो-लाङ्गूल, अस्, m. (fr. शुनः, gen. c. of
श्वन् + लाङ्गूल), N. of the youngest of the three
sons of Ṛcīka (or of the three sons of Ajīgarta,
according to the Aitareya-Brāhmaṇa; cf. शुनः-
पुच्छ).

1. शुन्य, अम्, n. (for 2. शुन्य see below), a
number of dogs or female dogs.

शुन्य 2. शुन्य, अस्, आ, अम् (more usually
[]
written शून्य, q. v.; for 1. शुन्य see p. 1014,
col. 3), empty, void; (अम्), n. a cypher.

शून्य शून्य, अस्, आ, अम् (probably connected
with शून above, fr. rt. श्वि), empty, void, hollow;
vacant, barren, non-existent; utterly destitute or de-
prived of, without (with inst.); ruined; nonsensical, un-
meaning; guileless, unsuspicious; indifferent; lonely,
private, desert, desolate, (शून्ये or शून्यम्, ind. in
a lonely place, secretly); bare, naked; (अम्), n. a
void, vacuum, blank; space, heaven, ether, the sky,
atmosphere; a dot, spot; a cypher; naught, vacuity,
nonentity, (one of the principles of Bauddha meta-
physics); N. of Brahma; (आ), f. a hollow reed; a
barren woman; the prickly pear; [cf. Gr. κενός,
κενεός; Æol. κέννος.]
—शून्य-गेह, अम्, n. an
empty house.
—शून्य-ता, f. or शून्य-त्व, अम्,
n. emptiness, voidness, vacuity, non-existence, un-
reality, the false or illusory nature of all existence.
—शून्य-पदवी, f. ‘empty path,’ the road or
passage of the soul, (see महा-पथ, मुद्रा-
मार्ग.)
—शून्य-मध्य, अस्, आ, अम्, having a
hollow centre, empty inside; (अस्), m. a hollow reed.
—शून्य-वत्, ind. like a cypher, annihilated or vanished
as it were.
—शून्य-वाद, अस्, m. the doctrine of the
non-existence of anything.
—शून्य-वादिन्, ई, m.
‘affirmer of non-existence,’ an atheist; a Buddhist.
—शून्य-स्थान, अम्, n. an empty place.
—शून्य-
हस्त, अस्, आ, अम्, empty-handed.
—शून्य-हृ-
दय, अस्, आ, अम्, ‘empty-hearted,’ unsuspecting,
unsuspicious; absent in mind.
—शून्याकृति (˚य-
आक्˚), इस्, इस्, इ, ‘empty-formed,’ having a vacant
appearance or aspect.
—शून्यागार-कृतालय (˚य-
आग्˚, ˚त-आल्˚), अस्, आ, अम्, making an abode in de-
serted houses.
—शून्यालय (˚य-आल्˚), अस्, m. an
empty or deserted house, (sleeping in such a house
is forbidden.)
—शून्यी-कृ, cl. 8. P. -करोति, -कर्-
तुम्, to make empty, leave.

शुन्ध् शुन्ध् (connected with rt. शुध्);
cl. 1. P. A. शुन्धति, -ते, शुशुन्ध,
शुशुन्धे, शुन्धितुम्, to purify, make clean or pure,
cleanse (P., according to some also A.); to be or be-
come pure, be purified, be cleansed (A.); cl. 10. P.
(according to some also A.) शुन्धयति (-ते), -यि-
तुम्, to purify, cleanse.

शुन्धा-वत्, आन्, अती, अत् (thought by some to be
fr. a lost Nom. शुन्ध्य, meaning ‘to desire purifi-
cation’), Ved. ‘possessed of desire for purification,’
sacred, holy, pure.

शुन्ध्यु, उस्, उस्, उ, Ved. ‘desirous of purifica-
tion,’ purifying; pure, bright; (उस्), m., N. of Agni
or fire, (according to Sāy. on Ṛg-veda I. 124, 4, an
Āditya or a kind of water-fowl); (उस्), f. a mare,
(the chariot of the Sun is said to be drawn by seven
mares); [cf. perhaps Lat. castus.]
शून-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, one who has increased.

सूनवत्, आन्, अती, अत्, one who has borne or pro-
duced; having budded or blossomed.

सुन्वत्, अन्, अती, अत्, pouring out libations, offering
sacrifice, sacrificing; (अन्), m. an offerer.
सुन्वत् सुन्वत्. See under rt. 3. सु.

सुन्वान, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. offering libations;
(अस्), m., N. of a son of Su-mantu.

सूनु, उस्, m. a son; a child, offspring; a daughter's
son; a younger brother; the sun; N. of the author
of the hymn Ṛg-veda X. 176 (having the patro-
nymic Ārbhava); (उस्, ऊस्), f. a daughter; [cf. Zend
hunu; Gr. υἱός; Goth. sunus, ‘a son;’ Angl. Sax.
sunu; Mod. Germ. sohn, &c.; see col. 1.]
सुनु सु-नु. See सु-नौ, p. 1121, col. 2.
सुनन्द सु-नन्द, &c. See p. 1121, col. 1.

सुनफा सुनफा, f. (= Gr. συναφή; cf.
अनफा), a particular conjunction of the planets.
—सुनफा-योग, अस्, m. the above conjunction.

सुनाकृत सुनाकृत, अस्, m. zedoary, Cur-
cuma Zerumbet (= कर्पूरक).
सुनाभ सु-नाभ. See p. 1121, col. 1.

सुनार सुनार, अस्, m. the udder of a bitch;
the egg of a snake; a sparrow.

सूनर सूनर, अस्, m. (probably for सु-
नर), Ved. a good or excellent man, (Sāy. =
शोभन-मनुष्य, Ṛg-veda V. 34, 7); ‘a good
leader,’ epithet of Soma, (Sāy. = सुष्ठु रात्रीणां
नेता, Ṛg-veda VIII. 29, 1); (ई), f., Ved. a good or
well-married or happy woman; epithet of the Dawn,
(Sāy. = जनानां सुष्ठु नेत्री, Ṛg-veda VII. 81,
1); (अस्, ई, अम्), well-disposed, friendly (Ved.).
सुनालक सु-नालक. See p. 1121, col. 1.

सुन्द् सुन्द्, a Sautra rt. meaning ‘to
shine, be bright.’

सुन्द, अस्, m., N. of a Daitya (son of Ni-sunda
and brother of Upa-sunda); N. of a Vānara or ape.
—सुन्दोपसुन्द (˚द-उप्˚), औ, m. du. the two
Daityas Sunda and Upa-sunda.

सुन्दर, अस्, ई, अम् (said to be fr. 5. सु with rt.
उन्द्), beautiful, handsome, lovely, charming, agree-
able; right; (अस्), m., N. of Kāma-deva; of a king;
of an author who lived in the beginning of the seven-
teenth century, (he composed the Abhirāma-maṇi
drama, the Dvādaśa-māsa-varṇana, and the Sundara-
śṛṅgāra); (ई), f. a beautiful woman; N. of a
daughter of Vaiśvānara; N. of a deity, (त्रिपुर-
सुन्दरी is apparently a form of Durgā); the tree
Heritiera Minor; turmeric; a kind of metre (= वि-
योगिनी); a particular Yoginī.
—सुन्दर-काण्ड,
N. of the fifth book of the Adhyātma-rāmāyaṇa;
of the fifth book of the Rāmāyaṇa.
—सुन्दर-
तरम्, ind. very well.
—सुन्दर-त्व, अम्, n.
beauty.
—सुन्दर-पुर-माहात्म्य, अम्, n., N.
of a part of the Brahmāṇḍa-Purāṇa.
—सुन्दरम्-
मन्य, अस्, आ, अम्, thinking one's self handsome
or beautiful.
—सुन्दर-शुक्ल, अस्, m., N. of the
author of the Mauna-mantrāvabodha.
—सुन्दर-
शृङ्गार, N. of a work on rhetoric by Sundara.
—सुन्दरी-तापिनी, f., N. of an Upa-niṣad belong-
ing to the Atharva-veda
—सुन्दरी-भवन, अम्,
n., N. of a temple.
सुन्दरक, अस्, m. a proper N.

सूनिन्, ई, m. one who keeps a slaughter-house, a
butcher, flesh-seller, one who causes the death of
animals, a hunter.

सूनृत सूनृत, अस्, आ, अम्, (thought to be
fr. 5. सु and rt. 1. नृत्), Ved. movable, quick,
active, brisk, lively, cheerful, kind, agreeable,
pleasant and at the same time true, (सूनृता वाच्
or गिर्, ‘cheerful words,’ or, according to some, ‘kind
yet sincere language,’ is one of the four things with
which even the poorest man is expected to greet a
guest, Manu III. 101; the sense ‘true’ may have
[]
arisen from some fancied connection with ऋत,
q. v.); fortunate, auspicious; dear, beloved; (आ), f.
true and agreeable speech, (Sāy. = प्रिय-हित-वाच्);
the goddess of true speech (= वाग्-देवता, Ṛg-veda
I. 40, 3, and invoked as a goddess in X. 141, 2);
excellent song; N. of Uṣas, (Naigh. I. 8); food
(= अन्न, Naigh. II. 7); N. of a wife of Uttāna-
pāda; (अम्), n. true and agreeable speech, pleasant
discourse; auspiciousness.
—सूनृत-वाच्, क्, क्, क्,
truth-speaking, speaking politely and truthfully.
—सू-
नृता-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, Ved. having a pleasant or
friendly voice, having excellent songs; (अती), f., N.
of Uṣas, (Naigh. I. 8.)
—सूनृता-वन्, आ, अरी, अ,
Ved. having a pleasant voice; (अरी), f. epithet of
Uṣas.
सून्मद सून्मद. See p. 1126, col. 2.
